design:
1. Who starts a session. Only the person: Start (the Start dialog, opened by Start or Continue on the project, Home's Continue and the palette), Approve and start on the plan card (and, at autonomy levels 0 and 1, Approve and start on the session plan card), Continue (CHF N more) on a budget card, Use API key on a credential card (D5: the person's yes to go on), 'start', 'run it now', 'go ahead and run it' and the like in chat or voice, the phone's start, Continue where it stopped on the stopped bar, a session's own Continue and the recovery Update's Continue. A start said in chat or voice is always read back once, at any budget and whether the parser or the chat model asked ('Start a session on Quote page (up to CHF 1.50)? [Yes] [No]'): today a start under USD 2 acts at once (session.ts:116-121). These carry by: 'person' on the scheduler's request; quiet hours never hold them. A person's Start pressed while the work waits for a Claude credential ('Start at 15:40') is a person start kept on the wait entry and made once at the reset (point 4). A schedule the person turned on (the monthly handover test) carries by: 'schedule'; quiet hours hold it like every start that is not the person's, as the setting says ('No notifications and no sessions that start on their own between these times'), and its fired key is written only when its start leaves the waiting line, so a job held by quiet hours still runs once afterwards, after a restart too. One exception, named in the ADR and asked of the owner: the critic's monthly calibration (ADR 0060, requirement H.7), a background job of the critic agent on no project, runs on its schedule as today (on by default, within its own monthly budget in Settings and the monthly cap); it does no project work, changes no task and never holds the person's agent or blocks Start (ADR 0102 point 4). The one other starter is the project setting 'When work is ready' (Settings, the project's rows, next to 'Who merges accepted work'): 'Wait for my Start' (the default for every project, new and existing) or 'Start a session by itself'. Turning it on asks a yes that says what it does ('Sessions of Quote page will start by themselves when work you made ready can run, up to CHF 5.00 each. Never in your quiet hours or while sessions are stopped.'); turning it off acts at once; only the person can change it (an agent actor's settings.set is refused; chat reads it back for a yes). With it on, a session of the project starts for work the person prepared, or that was theirs and can run again (a limit raised or reset, a Claude credential back), never for work only the agent prepared (D7's own tasks), with the project's session budget, after the same start check as the dialog (Stop all, no Claude, nothing runnable refuse it); quiet hours hold it ('It runs after your quiet hours.') and the start it owes is kept on the project (summary_cache.start_pending), so a Quit in the night does not lose it. CI results and PR comments (ADR 0075) start nothing, with the setting on or off: they go to the agent's inbox as today, for the next session to read (whether they should start a session with the setting on is an owner question).

2. Everything else only prepares work, through one function prepareWork(project, tasks, by) with by 'person', 'system' or 'agent': Inbox answers (Send answers, Go ahead without, Try again, Mark done anyway, Send it back, a sign-off's accept, the cannot-run card's Try again, the rebase card's I resolved it and Drop the branch, the rebuild card's Redo, a late approval's yes), the Tasks-row actions (Make ready, Try again, Resume, Go ahead without, Redo, Reopen), New task and chat's 'add a task' and Make this a task when the task is ready, chat's task moves (all by 'person'); a limit raised in Settings or reset by a new month for a task paused at it, and a Claude credential that serves again (its reset, the month, a raised allowance, a new key or sign-in) (by 'system'); and the agent's own new or changed tasks (D7, by 'agent'). prepareWork answers: (a) a session of the project runs: admit (point 3) says joined, no room or stopping; (b) none runs and the setting is off, or the preparation is the agent's: the task is ready for the person's next Start; (c) the setting is on and the preparation is the person's or the system's: a session starts, queues behind another project's, or waits for quiet hours (kept on the project). Each action then says in one line what happens next, in the daemon's words, after its own sentence (the Tasks row's change line, the Inbox Done line, chat's reply, the Settings change line): 'It joins the session that is running.' / 'Ready: it joins this session if budget is left after its own tasks, else your next Start.' / 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.' / 'Ready: it runs once you allow sessions again and press Start.' / 'A session started for it (this project starts by itself when work is ready).' / 'It runs after the session that is running now.' / 'It runs after your quiet hours.'; a task that still waits on another says 'It waits for "Create index.html" first; then ...' with the same clause. The Inbox's buttons say it before the press, read when the card is shown ('Back to ready with your note; it joins the running session if it fits.' or '...; it runs at your next Start.'). When nothing runs the Done line offers Start (that project's Start dialog) and the project's status line reads 'Ready: 3 tasks wait for your Start' with Continue. No notification, Update or reminder is sent for waiting work, however long it waits (the owner: 'We don't need notifications like that').

3. Prepared work joins a running session only if it fits (option C). The session's promise is what its Start dialog showed when it started: the ready tasks that fit the work budget (the session's budget less the fifth kept for reviews), then the tasks that follow them as they become ready, in run order while the work budget lasts. One function (promiseOf, start-check.ts) computes the dialog's list and the session's promise, so they are the same list; the runner records it (session.promised, and on the plan row). A session that began with every ready task (the setting, Continue where it stopped, chat's start) has the same computation at the moment it starts; Approve and start promises the approved plan's tasks and their followers; a session's Continue promises the remaining promise of the session it continues. A task is the session's own while the session can run it by itself (ready, running, in review, waiting only on the session's own tasks, or waiting for its Claude credential inside the session); once the person pauses or cancels it, or it needs the person's answer about it (a card after its retries, a question), it gives its room back, and bringing it back (Resume, an answer, Try again) asks again as a newcomer. A task that waited for its credential and is let back in by the person's Use API key (D5) is readmitted as the session's own (the runner's notAgain cleared for it). A newcomer (anything not promised) joins when what is left of the work budget now, less the remaining estimates of the session's own tasks (each estimate less what this session already spent on it, never below zero) and of what already joined, covers its estimate, priced as the planner prices it. Joined tasks run after the session's own queued tasks; a newcomer that did not fit is looked at again after each task ends, in priority order, so budget the promised tasks did not use is not wasted (owner: 'spare budget isn't wasted'). A task larger than the whole work budget (D4) never joins: it waits for a Start, whose dialog warns. A session that is stopping (Stop after this task), wrapping up at its budget, in its end review or closing takes nothing more ('Ready: it runs at your next Start.'): when its queue is empty the runner closes the admit handle before its last look for work, and a task admitted after that is kept out of the session, so no line says 'joins' for a session that ends without running it. The agent's own changes (D7) count like this: the parts of a split promised task stay the session's own up to that task's remaining estimate (a part beyond it is a newcomer); a step the agent adds before a promised task is a newcomer: it joins only if it fits, and if it does not, the promised task waits for it and leaves the promise, both named once ('Left for your next Start: "Check the links" (about CHF 0.20) and "Publish", which waits for it.'); a dropped duplicate frees its room; the agent's task check is paid only from the room left after the promise and what joined. At levels 0 and 1 the person's own preparation counts as approved for the session that runs (the person asked for that task); a task the agent adds needs the plan's approval (D7). Admitting never raises a budget and never touches the review fifth; a joined task whose estimate was short is held by the same caps as any task. The session page's log says each once: 'Took "Fix the header": you made it ready and it fits this session's budget.' / '"Add a share button" waits for your next Start: this session's budget is kept for its own tasks.'; the result names it once: 'Left for your next Start: "Add a share button" (about CHF 0.43).'
Edits: a task the session has not started yet is read fresh when it starts (wording, criteria, budget, review level and specialist; its estimate priced again); a running task is never changed mid-run: Edit is not offered for Running, chat's change of a running task is refused ('"Style the page" is running now: it is not changed mid-run; your note goes into its next attempt.') and the note it carried goes into its next brief.

4. A Claude credential that stops a task inside a session follows the person's credential policy (D5 decides which credential, whether to ask first and what a refusal does). Under 'next', or after the person's Use API key, the task goes on in the same session. Otherwise only that task waits (ADR 0100 point 10): the session goes on with the rest of its queue and ends 'Stopped to wait for a Claude credential' only when nothing else can run, and the wait entry on the billing source names the session, so its remaining promise and what is left of its budget stay known. At the stop's end (the reset, the month, a raised allowance, a new key or sign-in) the wake only prepares (the owner listed 'a credential coming back' among what prepares work): the tasks read 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.', the project's status line reads 'Ready: 2 tasks wait for your Start' with Continue, and the ended session's page offers Continue, which opens the Start dialog with the rest of that session's promise and its budget left (the session's cap less what the ledger booked for it, never more than the person gave); that session's first log line is 'Goes on with your session of 14:05.'. Nothing starts at the reset unless the project's hands-off setting is on or the person pressed Start or Continue during the stop: the dialog then offers 'Start at 15:40' ('Runs on your subscription once it is back; nothing moves before.'), that person start is kept on the wait entry (by 'person', the session it continues, its budget) and made once at the reset, after a restart too and never twice; the project's status line says 'Starts at 15:40 (your subscription's limit)' with Cancel; Cancel, Stop all and a newer Start of the project drop it. A task row of such a session reads 'Waits until 15:40 (your subscription's limit); then it runs at your next Start.' ('...; then your session goes on.' while a start is kept). Whether a session the person started should go on by itself at the reset is an owner question; built meanwhile: no. A wait entry without a session (made before this change) prepares the same way. The plan from a brief that waited is drafted again as today (no task runs; its card asks for the approval).

5. A running session is unmistakable everywhere (D8): one element, the run indicator, whose words come from the daemon (GET /running, a run.changed event on the stream and in polling, /health.running for the desktop shell): '[pulsing dot] Quote page · the coder works on "Style the page" · 4 min  [Stop ▾]'. It names the project and what the session does now in a few words ('plans the session', 'the coder works on "X"', 'the critic checks "X"', 'picks the next task', 'wraps up "X" at its budget', 'stops after "X"'), with '· then Garden site' when a person's start waits behind it. Clicking it opens the session page. Stop opens three choices, each with its line: Stop after this task ('Finishes the current task, then ends.'), Stop now ('Stops the current task at once; it goes back to Ready.', asked once), Stop all ('Stops every session; none starts until you allow it again.', asked once). It is a bar directly under the header on every page and at every width (never inside the collapsed menu), replacing the running chip and the separate red Stop all; the same component is Home's and the Overview's Working now, the first line of the Talk panel (a modal over the header) and the browser tab's title ('● Quote page · Forerunner'). The desktop shell shows the same words in the window title ('Forerunner — Quote page is working'), the tray tooltip's first line and the tray menu's first item (disabled), with 'Stop all sessions' and 'Allow sessions again' in place of 'Kill switch: stop everything' and 'Resume', and a blue dot on the tray icon while a session runs. Nothing shows when none runs; a start kept for a reset or held by quiet hours is not a running session and is said on its project instead. It follows the session live within one event (a task started or finished, the critic's review, a join, a stop request). Drafting the plan from a brief is not shown (the project's 'Drafting the plan…' line says it; the bench walk found Stop all during drafting confusing); the critic's monthly calibration is not shown (owner question). The project's status line (design §2) adds 'Starts at 15:40 (your subscription's limit)' with Cancel for a kept start, 'Starts after your quiet hours' for a held hands-off start and 'Starts after the session on "Quote page"' for a person's start that waits, and rule 4 reads 'Ready: 3 tasks wait for your Start' with Continue. The phone (apps/ui/src/mobile, phase H) reads the same words from GET /running later (ADR 0102); it is not built this round.

6. The rule for what the system does on its own (closes the owner question on Tasks-row actions): Redo, Try again, Reopen, Make ready and Resume never start a session; they prepare (point 2). Chat does the same when asked in words, read back once, with one Undo. On its own the system retries a task inside a running session up to the retry limit (design §4.3) and wraps up and pauses at a budget (ADR 0112, D4); it never starts a session without the person, except a start the person kept for a reset, the hands-off setting the person turned on and the critic's calibration named in point 1; it never reopens done or cancelled work, never retries past the limit, never raises a budget and never sends a reminder about waiting work.

7. Restart, money, security. Persisted: the setting (project settings), each wait entry with its session and a kept person start (billing source limits, version-checked), a held hands-off start (project summary_cache.start_pending), a session's promise (its plan row and the session.promised event), who started each session (plan.startedBy and the session.started event). Not persisted: a running session's joined list (a crash ends the session; recovery's Update offers Continue). After a restart nothing starts but what a line promised: a kept person start at its reset, a held hands-off start once quiet hours end, a schedule held by quiet hours. Every answer sync that runs at boot only prepares. Each session is its own row in the sessions list (D2), and one started by a session's Continue says whose session it continues. Card, chat, PR comment and page text never become instructions: prepareWork carries no text into a prompt except the person's own note, quoted as today; a kept start never calls a refused credential (it waits for a new one, D5); the hooks and the sandbox are not touched. Wave 8: on a shared project another person's prepared work goes through the same admit rule; the setting is the project owner's.
alternatives_rejected: Keep 'answering resumes work' (every answer that makes a task runnable starts or queues a session, today's resumeWork): rejected by the owner: "the user clearly states when a session will run, such that they could maybe queue up tasks and then change things and then also give some text context into the chat or to tell the project something and only then run a session. Because now it might run sessions when I'm in the middle of giving it instructions".

Let prepared work always join the running session (today's re-plan, room alone decides): it spends the budget the Start dialog promised to the planned followers, which then end 'Left for next time'; the owner chose option C: "the session keeps its promise and spare budget isn't wasted, I think that's probably the best.".

Never join (prepared work always waits for the next Start): wastes the spare budget of a running session and is not 'dynamic as much as possible' ("the management of the tasks should be able to feed into sessions that are already running when appropriate, and it should be dynamic as much as possible").

Decide the fit only when the session's queue empties and say 'it may join' at the action: the line would promise nothing checkable; deciding at the action and keeping the room for what joined makes 'It joins the session that is running.' true, and the re-check after each task keeps spare budget in use.
A grace period before a newcomer joins (so a person still shaping a task is not overtaken): rejected: the line says it joins at once, Pause holds it, and a timer makes 'when' unpredictable.

Keep the session row open ('paused') across a credential wait: the one-session-per-agent rule would block every other project's Start for hours or days (a weekly limit); the session ends and its Continue starts a new row with the budget left and the remaining promise.

Start a fresh session with the project's full budget when a wait ends (today): it starts work nobody asked to run then and passes what the person gave the session they started: "It should definitely not automatically do something even when told to wait or showing that it is waiting."

Let the person's session go on by itself at the credential's reset (this design's first draft: a continuation with a 'Don't go on' button): the owner's confirmed list puts 'a credential coming back' among what only prepares work, and it would start hours or weeks later (a weekly limit, the share's month) while the person may be giving instructions ("maybe I will also tell it things in between sessions"); asked as an owner question, and 'Start at 15:40' is the person's own way to have it go on then.

A reminder notification or status line after work has waited a few hours: the owner rejected it: "All this sounds good except the status line that notifies you if work has waited a few hours. I think that's not necessary. We don't need notifications like that".
One app-wide hands-off switch: per project lets one project run hands-off while another is still being shaped; an app-wide default for new projects is an owner question.

Keep the header's chip and the separate Stop all button and add more chips (Home, Talk, tray): several elements with different words; the owner asked for one clear signal everywhere and design §5 rule 10 keeps one place per fact.

Show drafting the plan in the run indicator: it is not a session the person started, has no Stop, and the bench walk showed Stop all during drafting confused the person; the project's line already says 'Drafting the plan…'.
Let CI results and PR comments keep starting sessions (ADR 0075): it is a start nobody asked for; the comment still reaches the agent's inbox for the next session, so nothing is lost.

Make 'Redo' and 'Try again' start a session (the session lead's earlier reading of option c): replaced by the owner's later answer that only the person's Start starts sessions; they now prepare and say what happens next.

At levels 0 and 1 keep every newcomer out of a running session: a Redo the person pressed is their own approval of that task; the autonomy level governs what the agent does without asking (the owner: 'the autonomy level deciding when it asks first'), not the person's own requests.

Let CI results and PR comments start a session when the hands-off setting is on: text someone else wrote would start paid work, and the yes line would promise less than the app does (design §5); asked as an owner question, built as prepare-only.

Count the agent's own new tasks (D7) as work that starts a hands-off session: the agent's check could then start session after session across sessions, beyond D7's limit of ten new tasks a session; only the person's preparation, or theirs made runnable again, starts one.

Keep quiet-hours holds only in the scheduler's memory: a Quit in the night (ADR 0094) would lose a held job for the month and a held hands-off start for good, while their lines said they run after the quiet hours.

decisions: S-1 Who asked is on every start: StartRequest.by = 'person' | 'schedule' | 'hands_off' (append-only; continues?: the session id a person start continues; trigger stays for the record), written on the session.started event and in the session row's plan JSON (plan.startedBy, append-only, no migration), which d1109-sessions words. Person starts: POST /sessions, session.start (chat, voice and phone), Approve and start (intake), Approve and start on the level 0/1 session plan card, Continue on a budget card, Use API key on a credential card (personStart / personContinue, called by d1109-cred-engine), Continue where it stopped, a session's Continue, the recovery Update's Continue, and a person start kept for a credential's reset. The daemon's Scheduler gets isQuietHours from a cached reader (QuietHours in compose.ts: notify_prefs.quiet_hours and the time zone, refreshed in the scheduler's refresh hook before every tick and when the settings route changes them; the port reads it synchronously); deferredNow holds every start that is not by 'person'; enqueue keeps every person start; a schedule's fired key is written when its start leaves the waiting line (started, or queued behind a session), never while quiet hours hold it. The critic's calibration is named in the ADR as the one exception (by 'schedule', as today). Why: the owner's control needs one fact the scheduler can enforce; the Quiet hours setting promises 'no sessions that start on their own'; a job held in the night must still run once.

S-2 One function prepares work: prepareWork(deps, {agentId, projectId, taskIds, reason, by: 'person' | 'system' | 'agent'}) in a new session/prepared-work.ts replaces resumeWork's start in every answer path (person-questions, cannot-run, findings, pr-answers rebase and Redo, late approvals) and returns {outcome, line}; recordStart stores the outcome on the card for its Done line. Outcomes: joined, no_room, stopping, waits_start, stopped_all, started, queued, deferred, nothing_to_run, failed. Why: one place decides and one map of words says it (design §5 rule 10), so no answer path starts a session by its own logic again.

S-3 Budget raises and resets prepare: wakeBudgetWaits withdraws the card and makes the task ready, then calls prepareWork (by 'system') instead of resumeWork; a raise through Settings (monthly cap, project budget, the subscription's allowance, whose share stop is d1109-cred-engine's) runs the wake at once and its change line says how many paused tasks are ready again and that they run at the next Start. Continue on a budget card stays a person start (personStart with the card's budget). Why: the owner: 'the user clearly states when a session will run'; a month reset can come weeks later, in the middle of the person's instructions.

S-4 CI results and PR comments start nothing, with the setting on or off: GitHostWatcher.fire no longer asks the scheduler; the events are delivered to the agent's inbox as today (deliver), the audit row records outcome 'waits_start', and the next session's brief reads them. Why: no start nobody asked for, and text a third party wrote never starts paid work; the information still reaches the next session (ADR 0075's content rule unchanged); whether the hands-off setting should let them start one is an owner question.

S-5 The hands-off setting: project.settings.start_by_itself, false by default for every project (no migration: absent is off); settings-view row 'When work is ready' with 'Wait for my Start' / 'Start a session by itself'; SETTING_SPECS entry (scope project, risk medium, narrows when off; turning on asks the yes with its effect line 'Sessions of Quote page will start by themselves when work you made ready can run, up to CHF 5.00 each. Never in your quiet hours or while sessions are stopped.'); settings.set refuses it for an agent actor. prepareWork and the budget and credential wakes read it; a start it makes is by 'hands_off', only for preparation by 'person' or 'system' (never by 'agent': D7's own tasks), with the project's session cap, after startBlocked (Stop all, no Claude, nothing runnable). A hands-off start held by quiet hours or queued behind another start is kept on the project (summary_cache.start_pending {since, why}, version-checked), asked again by a sweep in the scheduler's refresh hook once nothing holds it (after a restart too), and cleared when it starts. Why: the owner confirmed 'Only when you say so' as the default with the hands-off setting optional; per project so one project can run hands-off while another is shaped; a line that says 'It runs after your quiet hours.' must stay true across a Quit.

S-6 The promise is the Start dialog's list: promiseOf(check) in start-check.ts = runnable (cut as today) then later cut to the work budget left after runnable, in run order (the followers beyond it are named 'and N more wait for a later Start'); the runner computes the promise with the same function at its start (or takes the approved plan's tasks and followers, or, for a session's Continue, the remaining promise of the session it continues), emits session.promised {taskIds, estimateUsdMicro} and keeps it on the plan row. The dialog's sentence reads the cut list and adds one line 'Work you make ready while it runs joins it if its budget has room.'; while another project's session runs, 'Starts after the session on "Quote page"'. Why: 'the session keeps its promise' needs the promise to be what the person saw when they pressed Start.

S-7 Join only if it fits: a live-session registry (new session/live-sessions.ts) where the runner registers an admit handle for its project. admit(taskIds, by) reads each task fresh: the session's own (promised and runnable by itself, or waiting for its Claude credential inside the session) -> joined; stopping, wrapping up, in its end review or closing -> stopping (the line 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.'; the task is added to notAgain so it does not run in that session); an oversized task (estimate above the whole work budget, D4) -> no_room; else room = work budget less spent less the remaining estimates of its own tasks and of what joined; estimate (priced as the planner prices) <= room -> joined (kept in the session's joined map, session.joined event), else no_room. closing: when the queue is empty the runner sets the handle's closing flag before its last replan and clears it only if that replan found work, so an admit between an empty replan and the session's end never answers joined. readmit(taskIds) takes credential-waiting tasks back as the session's own and clears notAgain for them (d1109-cred-engine's Use API key). A task the person pauses or cancels, or that needs the person's answer, gives its room back; bringing it back is a newcomer. D7's changes: the parts of a split promised task are the session's own up to the task's remaining estimate (a part beyond it is a newcomer); a step added before a promised task is a newcomer, and if it does not fit the promised task leaves the promise and both are named once in the result; a dropped duplicate frees its room; the task check's cost is admitted like a newcomer (room after the promise and what joined). replan takes its own tasks first, then joined, then newcomers re-admitted in priority order after each task ends; nothing else (today's 'every ready task that fits'). At levels 0 and 1 a person's preparation is added to onlyThese when it joins; anything the agent adds is not. The result's 'Left for your next Start: ...' and two log lines (event-lines.ts) say it. Why: option C keeps the promise and uses spare budget; deciding at the action makes the line true; admitting never raises a budget.

S-8 Edits apply before a task starts and never during its run: at the claim the runner refreshes the queue item from the claimed row (specialist, title, estimate re-priced) before chooseSpecialist and the start line; task.update of a running task keeps refusing its field changes but queues the note it carries and answers '"X" is running now: it is not changed mid-run; your note goes into its next attempt.' (today the refusal drops the note). Why: 'queue up tasks and then change things': a change made before the run must be the run; a change mid-run would mix two briefs.

S-9 Every preparing action says what happens next: the commands that make a task ready (task.transition to ready, task.resume, task.reopen, task.create with status ready, which Make this a task uses) call ports.prepareWork after their transaction and append its line to the sentence (the Tasks row shows change.sentence already, chat replies with it); chat's read-back of such a move adds a preview of the line (ports.previewWork, read-only). The Inbox's card explains are read when the card is shown: RequestWordsContext gains running ('this_project' | 'other' | null) and startsByItself, so Try again reads '...; it joins the running session if it fits.' or '...; it runs at your next Start.'. Make ready's and Resume's static explains become 'Ready to run: the running session takes it if it fits, else your next Start.' and 'It is ready again: the running session takes it if it fits, else your next Start.'. Why: design §5 rule 4 (true now) and rule 9 (no promise the code does not keep); the owner wants to know when a session will run.

S-10 A credential stop's end prepares, and the person continues: the executor's noteWait passes the session id and the wait entry stores it ({projectId, agentId, since, sessionId}); at the stop's end credentialWaits.wake takes the entry and calls prepareWork(by 'system') for its project, so nothing starts unless the hands-off setting is on or a person start is kept on the entry. A person's Start, or a session's Continue, pressed while the stop lasts ('Start at 15:40') keeps one person start on the entry ({by 'person', continues, budgetUsdMicro}, version-checked; keepStartAtReset), made once at the stop's end, after a restart too and never twice; POST /projects/:id/continuation/cancel (Cancel), Stop all and a newer Start of the project drop it. A session's Continue (its page, the project status line, Home) opens the Start dialog with continues = that session: the remaining promise and budgetUsdMicro = its cap less the ledger's booked spend (no Continue when that is zero or less); the runner's first log line 'Goes on with your session of 14:05.'. personContinue(sessionId) and readmit(taskIds) are the ports d1109-cred-engine's Use API key calls. Row and card words: '...; then it runs at your next Start.' / '...; then your session goes on.' (a kept start). What a wait is, which credential serves next and whether the person is asked first stay D5's. Why: the owner's confirmed list puts 'a credential coming back' among what only prepares work; the person's own Continue keeps the promise and the budget they gave; whether a session should go on by itself at the reset is asked.

S-11 Chat says start in words, and every start said in chat or voice is read back: session.start gets askFromChat (a yes from chat and voice at any budget, whether the parser or the chat model asked; the app's, the palette's and the phone's starts are no chat); the parser also maps 'run it now', 'run them now', 'run it', 'go ahead and run it', 'let's run it', 'start it' (and the German 'starte es', 'jetzt ausführen') to session.start; negations ('don't run it yet', 'I'll run it later', 'not yet') and task text ('add a task: run the tests') do not. The chat model's tool definitions change: session.start ('Start a work session now on the person's say-so; it is read back for their yes; answers and task changes never start one'), task.reopen, task.resume and task.transition ('it is ready again: it joins the running session if it fits, else it waits for the person's next Start'), settings_set's new key line. Why: the owner named 'run it now'; 'ok' or 'sounds good' read by a model is not the person stating when a session runs; tool definitions are model-facing code and must say what the app does.

S-12 Words: one map in prepared-work.ts (preparedLine, preparedExplain) used by request-words.ts (startWords and the cards' explains and Done lines), task-words.ts (budget-paused and credential-wait rows), result.ts (paused and credential lines, the left-for-next-Start line), credential-wait.ts (after-the-wait sentences) and the commands' sentences; no person-facing sentence says 'by itself', 'starts a session' or 'goes on' unless the setting, a kept start or the person's own Continue makes it true. Why: design §5 rules 4, 9, 10; the owner: 'a sentence promises only what the app does'.

S-13 The ADR (next free number) records the rule, names the critic's calibration as the one exception, and amends 0053 (Approve and start on a session plan is a person start), 0060 (the calibration named as the exception; schedules held by quiet hours still run once), 0075 (CI and PR comments start no session; they reach the next session), 0088 (a late approval prepares; the next session consumes it), 0100 (a wait's end prepares; a session's Continue carries its remaining promise and budget; a person start kept for the reset), 0102 point 2 (Tasks-row actions prepare), 0112 (a raised or reset limit prepares; Continue is a person start), each amendment dated. Why: AGENTS.md: decisions go in ADRs; the session lead edits design core-experience.md from design_doc_changes.

packages/runtime/src/session/triggers.ts: a schedule's fired key is written before its start and a quiet-hours hold lives in memory, so a hold that outlives the process loses the start.

decisions: V-1 One run state in the daemon's words: a new daemon/run-indicator.ts computes RunningView[] ({sessionId, projectId, projectName, state, text, since, stop: ['after','now','all'], then?}) from the active sessions (not the chat's conversation row, not a plan being drafted, not the critic's calibration), their last task, review and stop events and the scheduler's waiting person starts; GET /running answers it, a run.changed event carries it on the stream and in polling, and /health gains running {projectName, text} (append-only) while activeSessions stops counting a plan being drafted. The words: 'Quote page · the coder works on "Style the page"', '... · the critic checks "X"', '... · picks the next task', '... · plans the session', '... · wraps up "X" at its budget', '... · stops after "X"', '· then Garden site' for a waiting person start; each at most 80 characters with titles shortened. runText is exported so d1109-sessions' working row says the same words. Why: one place per fact (design §5 rule 10); the phone later shows the same words (ADR 0102); the shell needs it without the UI.

V-2 One element on every page: RunIndicator, a bar directly under the header (role status, a pulsing dot, the words, the elapsed time, Stop ▾) on every route and at every width, never inside the collapsed menu, replacing RunningChip and the header's Stop all button; Stop offers Stop after this task (POST /sessions/:id/pause), Stop now (POST /sessions/:id/stop, asked once) and Stop all (POST /kill, asked once, 'Stops every session; none starts until you allow it again.'); the text opens the session; the store keeps it from run.changed; document.title reads '● Quote page · Forerunner' while it runs. The stopped bar, the no-key bar and the palette's Stop all question stay. Why: the owner: 'very visually clear no matter where the person is'; 'no clutter': one consistent element instead of two.

V-3 The same element elsewhere: Home's and the Overview's Working now render RunIndicator in its block form (same words, same Stop), and the project status line (project-status.ts, design §2) adds 'Starts at 15:40 (your subscription's limit)' with Cancel (a start kept for a reset, POST /projects/:id/continuation/cancel), 'Starts after your quiet hours' (a held hands-off start) and 'Starts after the session on "Quote page"' (a waiting person start), and rule 4 reads 'Ready: 3 tasks wait for your Start' with Continue. Why: design §3.2 and §3.4 keep Working now; the owner named 'Home, the project'; the project's one sentence says what waits and what will start.
V-4 Talk shows it: the conversation panel's first line is RunIndicator's compact form with Stop. Why: the modal covers the header.

V-5 The ended session's page says what comes next: a session that ended to wait for a credential shows one block 'Stopped to wait for your subscription's limit until 15:40: "B" and 1 more wait.' with Continue ('Opens Start with the rest of this session and the CHF 1.20 left of its budget.'); with a start kept for the reset it reads 'Starts again at 15:40 with "B" and 1 more.' with Cancel, then 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.' after it. Why: the person who opens that session can go on with what is left, or stop what they kept, there.

V-6 The Inbox's Done line offers Start when the answer prepared work and no session of that project runs (it opens that project's Start dialog); never while one runs. Why: the person's start is one click from where they answered, without a reminder.

Why: a minimised window or the tray is where a person looks when the window is not on screen; design §5 plain words.
V-8 The tray icon gets a blue dot while a session runs, drawn over the app's own icon at run time (no new asset). Why: the one signal visible without hovering, on Windows and Linux.
